title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
tasks_benchmarks: LIBERO-Plus (765 held-out Language Instructions variants + 360 other-category episodes)

headline_result.text: GPT-6 Astra's best edit (run C) changed 65 token-embedding rows of pi0.5 and raised held-out paraphrase success from 86.3% to 92.0% overall (74.3% to 87.5% on instructions containing edited tokens) with zero outcome changes on the 430 untouched instructions; all three independent sessions improved.
headline_result.quote: 65 embedding rows                              74.3% → 87.5% on targeted instructions                         430 other episodes: 0 changes

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 independent editor sessions; single held-out rollout seed (7)

key_claims.claim: The repair is local: all outcome changes fall inside instructions containing an edited token.
key_claims.quote: Run C improves edited-token instructions from 249/335 to 293/335 successes; all 430 untouched instructions retain their outcomes (411 successes).

key_claims.claim: Moving the same 65 rows by a matched-norm random direction does not help (85.2% vs 86.3% unedited).
A mechanical full replacement toward the editor's own destinations recovers much of the gain (90.5% vs 92.0% for the editor), and the direct difference is not significant.
Outside the three language repairs, the editor declined 12 of 13 candidates, and the one retained edit showed no significant held-out gain.
key_claims.quote: Of the other 13 sessions, 12 decline their candidates; the sole retained suffix follow-up has 𝑝 = .542.

key_claims.claim: The authors reconstructed MIT's released Qwen3.5-0.8B p50c edit and obtained a MATH-500 score close to the reported one.

notes_for_review: One of the most carefully controlled WSP studies: paired McNemar tests on a fixed 765-variant held-out split, three independent editor sessions, a matched-norm random-direction control, and an editor-informed dictionary (full replacement) control that explains much of the gain. The useful finding is narrow lexical repair (synonym-to-anchor embedding remapping), not new robot skills; 12 of 13 other attempts were declined. Gradient fine-tuning and prompt rewriting were not compared, and public code/weights were promised but not yet linked. It also reproduces MIT's Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500 edit (49.4% with one sample vs reported 48.1%), with a caveat about the unmatched baseline.
